summary: The milestone completed 5 experiments in 1.0 minute, including 3 compute-bound experiments. The Three-family GGUF load-envelope and teardown canary was the longest entry, but the data does not identify why; the immutable GPU field records no compute-task idle event.
bottlenecks_identified: The Three-family GGUF load-envelope and teardown canary was the longest entry, but no phase breakdown or causal evidence explains its duration.
The file-time reconstruction and near-zero recorded durations do not separate load, execution, and teardown costs.
The supplied evidence has no task-linked GPU trace or parallel-model runner receipt; the immutable GPU field is false, so this retrospective does not classify GPU idle as a bottleneck.
improvements_suggested: Record monotonic task and phase timings for model load, execution, and teardown.
Attach GPU utilization samples to each compute-bound task instead of relying on a single milestone-level snapshot.
Record the concurrent model count and selected runner at launch, and use DualGPURunner only when 2 or more models load in parallel.
Add an ownership-aware post-task cleanup path for GPU allocations that remain inactive after compute work.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add one task-owned lifecycle receipt with phase timings and GPU samples.
Release inactive GPU allocations after a guarded ownership and liveness check.
Log concurrent model count and runner selection for every compute launch.
meta_reflection: File-time order ranks the entries but cannot separate loading, execution, and shutdown work. A future nonzero savings claim needs task-linked timing, accelerator, concurrency, and runner receipts.
